statements.t: The Company anticipates that subsequent events and developments will cause the Company’s assessments to change.
We expect colocation revenue to increase as additional contracted capacity is commissioned and delivered to our customers and as we add new customer relationships over time.
Our hosted mining operations are expected to conclude by December 31, 2026, while we continue to wind down our self-mining operations.

The Senior Secured Notes and related guarantees are secured by first-priority liens, among other things, on substantially all assets of Core Scientific Finance and its subsidiary guarantors, which own or operate our specified data center development projects.

• On May 5, 2026, we closed on the acquisition of land and related electrical power in Hunt County, Texas for approximately $233 million in cash, which is expected to support approximately 430 MW of gross power capacity, with an approved ERCOT interconnection ramp schedule.

We expect colocation to represent an increasingly dominant share of our results as additional capacity is commissioned and delivered, gradually reducing our exposure to bitcoin spot price volatility and the operational risks associated with digital asset mining.

During the transition period, our consolidated results reflect both the ramp up of colocation revenue and the planned decline of our mining operations, and we expect this dynamic to continue as additional contracted capacity is placed in service.
Until that time, our financial results will continue to reflect our current dependence on CoreWeave as our primary source of colocation revenue.
As our colocation business grows and our mining operations wind down, the proportion of our cost base subject to direct power price exposure will decrease.
As our transition to colocation progresses, we expect bitcoin market conditions to have a diminishing effect on our overall financial results.
We will be opportunistic in monetizing our bitcoin holdings, subject to market conditions and our treasury strategy.
To the extent network difficulty increases materially or bitcoin transaction fees decline, the revenue and cash generation from our remaining fleet during the transition period will be reduced.
During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, tariffs contributed to higher costs for certain equipment and materials procured directly by the Company for non-customer-funded projects.

Our agreement with CoreWeave is funded almost entirely by the customer, and our financial contribution to those projects is capped at a fixed dollar amount, limiting our exposure to tariff-related cost increases on customer-funded capital expenditures.

However, capital expenditures associated with the AMD and Neocloud build-out, and other new data center development, are not subject to the same customer-funding structure as our existing CoreWeave conversion projects.

As of September 30, 2026, we had approximately $4.4 billion of expected future cash expenditures under outstanding purchase and construction commitments, of which approximately $202.2 million will be passed through to CoreWeave as invoiced.
Completing the AMD and Neocloud build-out is expected to require additional external financing and will depend on our ability to obtain financing on acceptable terms.
We will continue to manage our existing fleet with a focus on cash generation rather than competitive positioning, and we do not intend to make material new investments in mining capacity.
Our presentation of this measure should not be construed as an inference that its future results will be unaffected by unusual items.

Loss on disposal of property, plant and equipment increased by $15.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to disposal of assets in connection with the conversion of facilities from digital asset mining to HDC operations, including the wind-down of our mining operations, and write-offs of capitalized costs for certain development…

We expect these costs to decline as a percentage of revenue as our initial CoreWeave facilities reach full operational maturity, though we may incur similar costs in connection with bringing additional sites to operational status.

Customer prepayments under our CoreWeave colocation arrangements are associated with, and expected to offset a significant portion of, the capital expenditures required to build out and convert facilities for those arrangements.
We plan to complete project-level bond financing to fund capital expenditures associated with the AMD and Neocloud build-out.
We believe our existing liquidity, together with anticipated funding sources, will support the Company's planned development activities and expected operating requirements.

In connection with the Senior Secured Notes offering, we provided an uncapped completion guarantee for the benefit of the noteholders with respect to the completion of specified data center development projects.
This guarantee reflects our commitment to complete the specified development projects and is consistent with our existing contractual construction obligations, which are discussed further below.

The letter of credit facility may be used to issue letters of credit to provide credit support for specific project obligations under utility agreements and for other general corporate purposes, including in connection with our AMD and Neocloud data center development program.
We expect to use letters of credit under the letter of credit facility to replace cash collateral held in escrow accounts supporting utility obligations.
We will be opportunistic in monetizing our remaining bitcoin holdings, subject to market conditions and our treasury strategy.
We expect that completing the AMD and Neocloud build-out over the next 24 months will require additional external financing.
There can be no assurance that we will be able to obtain such financing on acceptable terms or at all.

estimates.name: Property, Plant and Equipment
estimates.t: Our mining-related property, plant and equipment involves significant estimates, including the determination of useful lives and the evaluation of recoverability and fair value.

estimates.name: Stock-Based Compensation
estimates.t: Compensation expense for these awards is recognized based on the estimated number of awards expected to vest, applying a cumulative catch-up adjustment when those estimates change.

estimates.name: AMD Warrant
estimates.t: Fair value is estimated using a Monte Carlo simulation model and required significant judgment, including assumptions about expected volatility, expected term, and the probability that the applicable vesting conditions will be satisfied.
